activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization

feedback.problem: The graph of the function $f(x)$ passes through $(3,-1)$ and ${f}^{′}(3)=2.$ Find $L(x)$, the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the graph of $f(x)$ passes through $(3,-1)$, we have that $f(3)=-1.$ Therefore, the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $a=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(3)+{f}^{′}(3)(x-3) \\  & =-1+2(x-3) \\  & =-1+2x-6 \\  & =2x-7.\end{aligned}
$$
